features.name: 3D Cube Renderer
features.description: R3F canvas with 27 cubelets colored from the cube state store. Drei OrbitControls for touch camera rotation; animated layer turns when stepping moves
features.evidence: 2026-10-28: /tutor's cube view is now 3D (src/components/cube3d/Cube3D.tsx, loaded by src/components/tutor/CubeView.tsx). 27 rounded cubelets with stickers colored from the store's facelets; drei OrbitControls (one-finger drag, no pan/zoom); camera distance fits the cube to any canvas shape. Next/Back animate one layer turn (0.28s, eased); taps mid-turn queue and play faster; jumps snap; prefers-reduced-motion snaps. Canvas draws only on change (frameloop=demand, dpr capped at 2). No WebGL or a failed load falls back to the old 2D CubeNet. three.js ships in its own lazy chunk (~247KB gz), not in /tutor's initial scripts. Logic in pure modules: src/lib/cube/geometry.ts (sticker positions, move -> axis/layers/quarter turns) and turnAnimator.ts (turn queue + followCubeStore). ./init.sh passed (typecheck, lint, 134/134 tests incl. 58 geometry tests proving the turned layers land on cubejs's state for all 54 moves, 10 animator tests, 3 CubeView tests; next build, /tutor static). Playwright (SwiftShader WebGL) on next start: renders at 390x844 light/dark and 375x667, mid-turn frame shows the D layer turning, drag orbits the camera, 8 rapid taps + 2 Backs give a pixel-identical canvas to slow taps, all 32 moves end on a solved cube, reduced motion shows the final state within 60ms, no horizontal scroll, no console errors (one THREE.Clock deprecation warning from inside R3F).

features.name: Manual Facelet Entry
features.description: Interactive 6-face grid where the user taps facelets to set colors, with validation that the result is a legal cube state. Doubles as the scanner's correction screen

features.name: Roux Solver: First Block
features.description: Generate a human-style move sequence that builds the left 1x2x3 block (FB). No Kociemba output
features.evidence: 2026-10-28: src/lib/solver/ (pieces.ts, search.ts, firstBlock.ts). solveFirstBlock(state) builds FB the Roux way and returns named steps: optional whole-cube rotation (orange left, yellow down), the yellow-orange DL edge, then for each corner-edge pair (shorter order first): free the pieces if stuck on the left side, join corner and edge using only U/R/r/M (never touch the left side), insert the joined pair with face turns while it stays joined every move. Each phase is as short as possible (IDA* over tracked pieces with distance tables); ties go to the easiest moves (moveEffort). No Kociemba. Random cubes: ~9.9 moves on average (vs ~9.2 for plain shortest steps), max 15 over 300; median 0.6ms, first solve ~250ms (builds tables). ./init.sh passed (typecheck, lint, 149/149 tests incl. 15 new: move tables match cubejs for all 24 search moves; 100 seeded scrambles check every phase (free leaves both pieces reachable, join uses only U/R/r/M and ends joined, insert keeps the pair joined on every move, DL edge and finished pairs stay home after each step); exact free/join/insert for F' U R U' F; rotated and M-offset cubes start with a rotation; next build). Revised after owner review: the first version solved each pair as a plain shortest search, which didn't teach pairing. Not wired into /tutor yet: the demo lesson stays hand-written until SB/CMLL/LSE exist.
